title: Cycle Capacity Decision Lab: Staffing, Deep Cuts, and Contingency Ledger
creator: Maya Torres
description:
Summary: Run a lightweight, repeatable 'Decision Lab' for the upcoming cycle to (1) quantify available engineering capacity across PM/Eng/Design; (2) prioritize work by customer impact and risk; (3) produce a set of recommended deep-slice scope cuts and contingency reserves; and (4) publish a one-page ledger that the execs and triage leads can use mid-cycle.

Background: We consistently under-index scope cuts mid-cycle and lack a single canonical ledger for reserves. This causes firefighting and ad-hoc deprioritization that impacts SLAs and roadmap predictability. This ticket creates the playbook and runs the first trial for the March cycle, producing artifacts for cross-functional sync.

Goals / Acceptance criteria (must satisfy all):
- A published Decision Lab runbook (Confluence) with step-by-step facilitation guide and templates.
- A completed capacity ledger for the March cycle that lists committed headcount-hours per initiative, named reserves (hours and percentage), and 3 candidate deep-cut slices per initiative.
- Triage rubric that maps severity/customer-impact to minimum staffing and fallback policy.
- Executive one-pager and a short demo to GTM and Eng leads.

Deliverables:
- Confluence doc: Decision Lab runbook + templates (link below).
- Spreadsheet: Capacity ledger (committed vs available, buffer lanes, risk-adjusted hours).
- Short recorded walkthrough (5–8 mins).

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: PM/ENG/DES planning for the cycle, template creation, initial trial run, one-pager for execs.
- Out of scope: Changing hiring plans, long-term org-level rebalancing, payroll or headcount requests.

Proposed approach (3 options considered):
1) Top-down carve: Execs set a fixed percent reserve (e.g., 15%) and PMs carve scope to fit. Fast but can lead to misaligned priorities.
2) Bottom-up ledger: Engineers and PMs estimate commit; central triage creates reserve lanes and recommends cuts. More accurate but heavier facilitation.
3) Hybrid Decision Lab (recommended): PMs submit conservative committed hours; Decision Lab facilitates a 90-min session to reconcile across teams, produce reserve lanes, and vote on deep slices. Balances speed and accuracy.

Tradeoffs and rationale:
- We choose the hybrid model because it gives participation and buy-in while keeping facilitation time bounded. It also produces artifacts that can be re-used.
- Risk: Estimates will be noisy. Mitigation: apply a 20% risk factor to feature work and enforce a minimum reserve lane.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- PM leads: Maya Torres (creator), Ethan Park (assignee), Julianne Reed (stakeholder)
- Eng leads: Priya Nambiar, Carlos Ortega
- Design lead: Noor al-Hassan
- Finance/Revenue partner: Aaron Feldman (for customer-impact calibration)

Links to artifacts: 
- Decision Lab runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CYCLE/Decision+Lab+Runbook+Draft
- Capacity ledger (spreadsheet): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1CapacityLedgerMarch2026
- Example PR with template export: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3421
- Dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/capacity-metrics/march-2026

Notes about measurements:
- We'll track the following KPIs for success: fraction of committed work delivered by end of cycle (>85% target), number of mid-cycle scope reassignments (target < 2), and time to remediate critical incidents where reserve lanes were used (target < 48 hours).

Acceptance criteria for 'complete':
- Runbook published and reviewed by PM/Eng/Design leads.
- Ledger uploaded and validated by Eng leads.
- Exec one-pager shared and a 15-min sync scheduled.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Kickoff meeting: aligned on hybrid Decision Lab approach. Priya requested clearer definitions for 'buffer lanes' vs 'surge lanes'. Action: add glossary to runbook. (Maya)

2026-03-03 — Engineering estimates collected from squads; variance observed on infra tasks (range 2x). Agreed to apply a default 20% risk multiplier to feature estimates and 35% to infra/ops items. (Ethan)
2026-03-05 — Draft ledger uploaded to spreadsheet. Julianne suggested adding customer-severity tags (P0/P1/P2) and mapping to minimum headcount. Added new column. (Julianne)
2026-03-07 — Design review: Noor flagged one initiative (UX search rewrite) as high-effort; proposed splitting into 'MVP search' + 'polish' slices to enable a safe deep-cut. (Noor)

2026-03-09 — Decision Lab trial facilitation: 90 minutes. Outcomes: identified 3 deep cuts totaling 180 engineer-hours, agreed on 12% reserve lane, and created 'contingency ledger' tab for mid-cycle use. Meeting notes and votes recorded in Confluence. (Maya/Ethan)
2026-03-11 — Executive sync: presented one-pager. Execs approved the 12% reserve with a trigger to top up to 18% if two P0 customer incidents occur. (Aaron)
2026-03-12 — Follow-up: UX search MVP split assigned as sub-issue PM-88625. Ran a retro on Decision Lab facilitation; action to shorten ballots and add a pre-read template. (Maya)
